naming_clarity.reason: The capability sentences stay in fleet-operator vocabulary, but the closing paragraph switches to internal V-model process language - 'This stream', 'its architecture is drafted', 'the workflow asks for the choice' - which a fleet operator cannot confirm and which does not describe the capability at all.
naming_clarity.suggestion: Drop or move the closing paragraph: the make-or-buy state belongs in the sourcing decision record (or the architecture element that carries the open choice), not in the story body. If the sourcing route must be visible here, say it as 'how the current is sensed is not yet decided' in capability terms.

no_mechanism_leak.reason: No class, function, module, table, internal endpoint or committed technology appears. Contactors, busbars, pack fuse and state of charge are physical/domain objects, and the sensing principle is explicitly left undecided ('built in-house or bought as a supplier module'), so no tech choice is named.

parent_fit.reason: user_story is the root stage of this project V and carries no outgoing parent link, so per the pack scoring guide this axis is fully met by default.

single_user_capability.reason: Two independently deliverable capabilities get equal billing: a trustworthy state-of-charge figure from accurate current measurement, and a fast overcurrent cutoff that protects cells and busbars. They have different purposes (accounting vs protection), different observation surfaces (charge drift at the next full charge vs contactors opening on a short circuit) and the story itself decomposes into two requirements at different integrity levels (REQ_CURRENT_ACCURACY QM, REQ_OVERCURRENT_DETECTION ASIL C) - proof that either could ship without the other.
single_user_capability.suggestion: Split into two stories: (1) know how much current flows through the pack accurately enough that the reported remaining charge does not drift from the value measured at the next full charge; (2) interrupt a short-circuit current before it damages cells or busbars, evidenced by the contactors opening instead of the pack fuse tripping. Keep the shared measurement basis in the downstream requirements.

user_observable.reason: Both claims are checkable from outside the pack: the reported state of charge is compared against the value measured at the next full charge, and a short circuit is observed as contactors opening rather than a blown pack fuse.

summary: One capability pair fused into a single story: accurate current measurement for charge accounting and fast overcurrent protection are separately deliverable (and separately decomposed downstream at different ASIL levels). Observable and mechanism-free, but the closing paragraph is process commentary in internal vocabulary. 7/10.
